heard: Sitting Bull saw the soldiers falling long before they arrived. In June 1876, George Custer rode toward the Little Bighorn. Crow scouts warned him that the village was unprecedented. Custer ignored them, unaware a supporting army had already retreated. He split his regiment to prevent the families from scattering. A final desperate note begged for reinforcements that never came. Over 200 cavalrymen were annihilated on a ridge within an hour. Sitting Bull's vision of falling soldiers had come true.
